A woman carries a pot on her head and a baby on her back through Teli village. Many ancient mud buildings line the Bandiagara escarpment in the background.
Three boys sit beneath the Bandiagara escarpment at Teli village. Ancient mud buildings and tombs carved into the cliff can be seen above them.
Detail of the skirt wrap of Halimata Traouré, indigo dyer. The indigo-dyed textile has stripes in different shades of blue.
Women sit in Baramandougou mending calabash vessels and plastic buckets by stitching the cracks.
A man sells striped indigo-dyed cloth at a stall in Fangasso market.
View across Fangasso market. People crowd through the street and the packed stalls. In the foreground a woman with a baby strapped to her back bends over among sacks of produce.
View of a baby strapped to its mother's back by a blue and white striped indigo-dyed cloth, in Fangasso market.
An indigo-dyed cloth hangs in a stall in Fangasso market. The textile has resist-dyed patterns of pale yellow squares and rectangles against a dark blue ground.
Detail of Kani-Kombole mosque. Sets of three carved palm sticks project from the adobe walls at regular intervals.

A woman dyes with wild indigo in Kani-Kombole village. She mixes the indigo solution in a broken pot, with a tied bunch of Indigofera arrecta in front of her and a bucket of millet stalk ash to her left. Indigo-dyed yarns hang up behind her.

A woman beats indigo-dyed cloth in Kani-Kombole village. She has laid the folded cloth onto a log and beats it with a wooden beater. In the foreground is a broken pot containing the dye solution, two lumps of dried indigo dye and a bundle of wild Indigofera arrecta. Indigo-dyed cloths and yarn hang up behind her.

View of an indigo-dyeing yard in Enndé village. A woman dips cloth in a dye solution contained in a round pot. Indigo-dyed cloths hang to dry on a line nearby. The Bandiagara escarpment towers up in the distance.
Painted tombs, the 'Hogon burial area' in the Bandiagara escarpment at Teli. The mud constructions are painted with triangles in black, white and ochre.
View of the Bandiagara escarpment between Teli and Enndé villages. Small mud granaries with thatched roofs are visible at the base of the escarpment.

Granary door and lock in Teli village. The small wooden door is set into a square opening in the mud structure. The lock comprises a wooden bracket with two carved wooden figures on top and a wooden horizontal bolt.
Portrait of a woman who assists in childbirth and performs circumcisions. She wears an indigo-dyed skirt with stitch-resist designs and colourful thread embroidery, and carries a baby on her back.
View of a wooden toilet door in Teli village, carved with many human figures in relief. The door is set into a mud brick wall.

A woman dyes cloth with wild indigo in Kani-Kombole village. She holds a scrap of material which has been dipped in the dye substance inside a broken pot. A bundle of wild Indigofera arrecta lies behind the pot.
Climbing up the Bandiagara escarpment.
People on donkeys, described as 'Touareg slaves' on the way to Bandiagara.
People with heavily laden donkeys, on the way to Bandiagara. Described as 'Touareg slaves'.
Portrait of two men identified as 'healers', near Djiguibombo. The two men wear brown over-garments, with the man on the left wearing a brown cap and the man on the right a pale blue knitted hat.
Detail of an indigo-dyed cloth, an 'old lady's indigo wrap'. Strips of plain indigo-dyed textile are sewn together.

Mud brick granary in Yasso. The small square structure, which sits atop a base of logs and stones, curves inwards towards a conical thatched roof. Two small human figures have been formed from mud on one of the walls.
Group of young Dogon boys and a young woman standing under a large tree. The young woman is wearing an indigo skirt and a variety of necklaces including a Maria Theresa thaler pendant.

View of a Dogon village 30 miles west of Koro. A peaked mud structure on the left is probably a mosque, and various mud buildings with flat and peaked straw roofs are situated to the right, probably homes and granaries, surrounded by a straw fence. A small field of millet is growing outside the village. A pair of women and a child are gathered under the tree in the foreground.

A Dogon family, including a man wearing a white tunic and cap, a young woman wearing an indigo skirt various necklaces, yellow drop earrings and a silver headband, and two young boys. The family are standing near mud huts and granaries with straw roofs in a village 10 km east of Bandiagara.

A Dogon woman, carrying a small child on her back, grinding sorghum in a large dug out vessel under the shade of a tree. A pile of sorghum, waiting to be ground, is piled up in the foreground next to baskets and pestles.
View of a Dogon settlement near Koro. A large herd of goats is gathered outside the settlement which is made up of a peaked mud structure (possibly a mosque), peaked straw huts and adobe buildings.
View of part of a Dogon village, 10 km east of Bandiagara. Consisting of mud and stone walls and raised mud huts with peaked straw roofs, probably used to store grain.

A young Dogon boy and a woman standing in the doorway of a mud home in a village near Bandiagara. The woman is wearing an indigo skirts and a variety of beaded necklaces including a Maria Theresa thaler pendant and yellow drop earrings. Around her head she has a silver beaded headband, and her hair is braided with a single braid draped over her forehead. Her lower lip is pierced with a silver ring.
View of a Dogon village 10 km east of Bandiagara made up of a a large group of peaked straw roofed huts and stone walls.

View of a Dogon village near Koro. A peaked mud structure on the right is a mosque, and various mud buildings with flat and peaked straw roofs are situated behind, probably homes and granaries. A large herd of goats is gathered outside the village.
View of a woman walking through a Dogon village 10 km east of Bandiagara, with stone walls and peaked straw roofed granaries.
A group of Dogon men and boys stood in front of a truck, probably Edward Ross's truck, 30 km west of Koro.

A group of Dogon women wearing indigo skirts are lifting water from a well in a village 20 miles west of Koro. Two of the women, one carrying a baby on her back, are using a pulley system to help them lift the water from under ground.
View of a lane with mud and peaked straw roofed huts in a Dogon village 10 km east of Bandiagara.
Ancient mud dwellings beneath the Bandiagara escarpment at Teli.

A young Dogon woman and boy pounding millet in a doug-out vessel in a village 10km east of Bandiagara. Behind them is a peaked straw roofed mud hut, raised off the ground, possibly used to store grain.
Portrait of a smiling seated Dogon woman wearing an indigo skirt and head scarf. She is wearing a red beaded necklace and yellow drop earrings.

Portrait of a Dogon man sitting on a stone wall in a village near Bandiagara. The man is wearing a green cap, a white tunic and various twisted metal armlets and a metal ring. Resting on a rock next to him is his smoking pipe.

A group of Dogon women wearing indigo skirts are lifting water from a well in a village 20 miles west of Koro. One of the women, carrying a baby on her back, is using a pulley system to help her lift the water from under ground.

View of a group of granaries in a Dogon village near Koro. The granaries are mud huts raised off the ground with peaked straw roofs, most of which have a pair of storks nesting on top of them. A small herd of goats are grazing in the foreground.

View of a Dogon village near Koro. A peaked mud structure in the centre is a mosque, and various mud buildings with flat and peaked straw roofs are situated behind, probably homes and granaries. A large herd of goats is gathered outside the village.

View of a Dogon village 10 km east of Bandiagara. A mosque with a tall peaked mud roof sits behind a group of mud a straw huts and granaries. In the foreground are two wooden mortars and a wooden pestle used for grinding grain.

Portrait of a young Dogon woman wearing a variety of beaded and pendant necklaces including a Maria Theresa thaler pendant and yellow drop earrings. Around her head she has a silver beaded headband, and her hair is braided with a single braid draped over her forehead. Her lower lip is pierced with a silver ring.

Portrait of a young Dogon woman wearing a variety of beaded and pendant necklaces including a Maria Theresa thaler pendant and yellow drop earrings. Around her head she has a silver beaded headband, and her hair is braided with a single braid draped over her forehead. Her lower lip is pierced with a silver ring.

A Dogon man wearing a white tunic and green cap and with a smoking pipe in his mouth, is standing in a village 10 km east of Bandiagara. Around him are various wooden pots and baskets and a peaked straw roofed building that is possibly a granary. A young woman and two children are standing in the shade of a wooden lean-to attached to a mud house.

Portrait of a Dogon woman wearing a variety of beaded necklaces including a Maria Theresa thaler pendant and yellow drop earrings. Around her head she has a silver beaded headband, and her hair is braided with a single braid draped over her forehead. Her lower lip is pierced with a silver ring.

Portrait of a Dogon woman wearing a variety of beaded necklaces including a Maria Theresa thaler pendant and yellow drop earrings. Around her head she has a silver beaded headband, and her hair is braided with a single braid draped over her forehead. Her lower lip is pierced with a silver ring. She is a holding a large wooden pestle, presumably for grinding grain.

Portrait of a Dogon woman and child. The woman is carrying a large white bowl containing blue and white cloths on her head. Her hair is plaited into two braids, which are tied beneath her chin. Her ears are pierced with large red and yellow decorative hoop earrings, and she has a gold nose ring and various necklaces.

A Dogon woman, carrying a small child on her back, grinding sorghum in a large dug out vessel. More sorghum, waiting to be ground, is kept in a basket next to her. The woman is wearing an indigo skit, and a red, yellow and green bead necklace and white hoop earrings.
View of part of a Dogon village, 5 miles east of Bandiagara. Consisting of mud and stone walls and raised mud huts with peaked straw roofs, probably used to store grain.
A Dogon woman stands next to various bowls under the shade of a tree, behind her are raised granaries made from mud and peaked straw roofs from a village 10 km east of Bandiagara.
Mud brick granaries in Dogo-Dogo village. One smaller and one larger square building are pictured, each supported by a base of logs and stones. The smaller hut has a conical thatched roof.
Portrait of Halimata Traouré, indigo dyer.
Millet growing in a field in Dogon country, Mali.
View through Fangasso market. People walk through the crowded streets, while all sorts of textiles and clothing hang from the awnings of stalls.
View of horses and colourfully painted carts at Fangasso market. In the background is an adobe fortified structure with bundles of palm fronds projecting from the walls, possibly the town's mosque.
Group of newly circumcised boys at Tonségué. Many of the boys wear long robes of blue or green and hold wooden clapper devices.
